# Capability catalog

Every input a composition can declare, and every input the build discovers without being told.
Generated from `src/catalog/surface.ts` and the constants in `src/manifest/sidecar.ts`; each row's
`verified` column states how far this repository has actually checked it — `probed` means a
violation was constructed and the implementation rejected it, `pinned` means the stated literal was
found in the named source file and nothing more.

Sidecar rows are probed against `parseSidecar` and name the diagnostic they produce. Animation
rows are probed against the vendored compiler, which has no diagnostic codes and refuses by
throwing, so those rows own none. Layout findings are neither: they are read off a rendered
frame, own no diagnostics, and are probed by handing `findingsFor` a geometry copied out of
`compositions/layout-codes` and asserting the codes it returns.

| regular | yes | — | string relative path to the regular face; same path rules as footage src | src/manifest/sidecar.ts:464 | probed |
| bold | yes | — | string relative path to the bold face; same path rules as footage src | src/manifest/sidecar.ts:464 | probed |
| faces | no | — | optional object of name -> { regular, bold }: named faces a class literal selects with `font-[name]`. A name matches /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ (the class token's own rule), at most 8 faces, both weights required per face, same path rules as footage src. The build bakes every (size, weight, face) a literal uses into its own slot, all faces sharing the core's 128-slot table (19 pinned for the default pair and mono, 109 dynamic). `resolveComposition` refuses declared font files totalling more than 64 MiB, default pair included, each distinct file once | src/manifest/sidecar.ts | probed |

| animate-<name> | no | — | binds a theme.animation entry to the node; a name no theme declares is refused and the message lists the declared names. The refusal needs evidence that the literal IS a class, because every string literal in the module reaches this parser: either the literal was the whole value of a JSX class= attribute, which the collector records (patches/0012), or some other token in it parsed. Neither holds for a class built by concatenation or interpolation — an operand of + and a quasi of an interpolated template are never the whole value, are not recorded, and still drop silently. A backtick with nothing interpolated into it IS the whole value and is recorded | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts:592 | probed |

## Paint (class literals — faces, text effects, gradients, filters, blend modes)

| key | required | default | constraint | source | verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| font-[name] | no | — | selects the named face `name` from the sidecar's `fonts.faces` for this node's text. Every (px, weight, face) triple gets its own atlas slot, allocated after the pinned table in first-sight order; a face takes precedence over `font-mono`. A name no `--font-face-*` flag declared fails the BUILD (bake-font.ts: "names a face this build does not declare"), not the compile, because the compiler has not seen the sidecar. `openMeasurer` measures per face: `sizes: [{ px, bold, face }]`, `measure(px, bold, face)` | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| text-stroke-[Npx] \| text-stroke-<color> \| text-stroke-outside\|center | no | no stroke; outside | an outline around a Text node's glyphs. Width `text-stroke` (1px), `text-stroke-N` or `text-stroke-[Npx]`, at most 64 px; colour `text-stroke-<palette>` or `text-stroke-[#hex]`, transparent by default, so a width alone draws nothing. `outside` (default) grows outward and is painted under the fill; `center` straddles the glyph edge and is painted over it. With `text-transparent` the stroke is hollow text: the ring only. Width and colour animate in keyframes as `textStrokeWidth`/`textStrokeColor` (or `-webkit-text-stroke-width`/`-color`). Paint only — layout never grows for it, so an outside stroke is ink past the box (`text_box_overflow`). Coverage is a distance field over the run's own rasterised coverage, drawn by this repository's rasteriser only (patches/0017, class motion, op 66) | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| blur-sm\|md\|lg\|xl\|2xl\|3xl \| blur \| blur-none \| blur-[Npx] | no | 0 (no layer) | a gaussian blur of the node AND its subtree as one layer (CSS `filter: blur()`); the value is the standard deviation in px — Tailwind v3 steps 4/8/12/16/24/40/64 — at most 128. Keyframe-animatable as `blur` or as `filter: "blur(Npx)"`, continuous in the deviation. Computed at 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 resolution from 8, 16, 32 px of deviation; crossing one of those moves a channel by at most 2 levels (core test, measured 1). The blur spreads inside the clip in force at the node, never past it. No background blur. Inside a perspective (3D) subtree it is ignored. patches/0018, class motion, ops 67/68 | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| drop-shadow-[X_Y_B_#hex] \| drop-shadow-<color> \| text-shadow-… \| glow-[B] \| glow-<color> \| glow-gain-[N] | no | none (colour transparent); gain 1 | a shadow of the node and its subtree made from their alpha (CSS `drop-shadow()`): offset X, Y and blur RADIUS B in px (deviation B / 2, as CSS), at most 256; the colour as the fourth value or as `drop-shadow-<palette>`/`-[#hex]`, transparent by default, so geometry alone draws nothing. `text-shadow-` is the same props under CSS's name for text; `glow-[B]` is a shadow at offset 0 with its own `glow-<color>`; `glow-gain-[N]` (0..16) multiplies the blurred alpha, clamped, which thickens a glow. Offsets round to whole physical px. Every value is keyframe-animatable as `dropShadowX/Y/Blur/Color/Gain` or as `filter: "drop-shadow(x y b color)"`. The shadow sits under the node, inside the clip in force at it. patches/0018, class motion | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| mix-blend-normal\|multiply\|screen\|overlay\|plus-lighter\|add | no | normal (no layer) | composites the node and its subtree, as one layer, over what is beneath by the W3C separable blend function, then source-over (CSS `mix-blend-mode`). `plus-lighter` and `add` are linear dodge, min(1, backdrop + source), composited like the others rather than as a Porter-Duff plus. Integer on 0..255 channels. patches/0018, class motion | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| via-<color> \| from-N% via-N% to-N% \| bg-linear-N \| bg-linear-[Ndeg] \| bg-linear-to-t\|r\|b\|l \| bg-radial \| bg-[linear-gradient(…)] \| bg-[radial-gradient(…)] | no | legacy two-stop gradient | a gradient ground with up to six stops (from, four vias, to), at any angle in CSS's convention (0deg = to top, 90deg = to right) or radial (the farthest-corner ellipse about the centre; no other shape or centre). Stops in an arbitrary gradient are `#hex` or palette names with an optional `N%`, `_` for a space, positions fixed up as CSS does; `via-<color>` alone sits at 50%. A literal with only `bg-gradient-to-* from-* to-*` keeps the two-stop path word for word. Interpolated premultiplied, so a stop fading to transparent keeps its colour. The gradient follows the node's transform, and fills the inside of a rounded border. Angle, stop colours and stop positions animate as `gradAngle`, `gradFrom`, `gradTo`, `gradVia1..4`, `gradFromPos`, `gradToPos`, `gradVia1Pos..4Pos`. patches/0019, class motion, ops 69/70 | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |
| bg-clip-text \| bg-clip-border | no | border | on a Text node, paints the node's ground into its glyphs instead of its box — the gradient (legacy or not) or the solid `bg-*` colour — and the text colour is not drawn, so the Tailwind idiom `bg-clip-text text-transparent bg-linear-90 from-… to-…` is gradient text. The gradient spans the node's box. A stroke is not painted by it. patches/0019, class motion | vendor/pocketjs/framework/compiler/tailwind.ts | probed |

## Declaring footage (generator side — `src/footage/declare.ts`)

| key | required | default | constraint | source | verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tileNodes / footageTrack | no | — | the one way footage tiles are declared. `tileNodes` emits one <Image debugName=… class="absolute left-… top-… w-[Npx] h-[Npx]"> per cell and `footageTrack` emits the sidecar entry, both derived from ONE drawn width and height — including `grid`, which is therefore never typed. A track is one fact written twice and the drawn size IS the ingested size, so an edit that moves both consistently stretches the picture rather than failing | src/footage/declare.ts:63 | pinned |
| hand-written tile name (warned) | no | — | `lint` WARNS with `footage.tileNamedByHand` when a `<nodePrefix>/tile:<col>:<row>` name for a prefix the sidecar DECLARES appears in a string or template literal it cannot attribute to `tileNodes`. A generated file is excused when the gen.ts beside it holds no such name; a generator that builds the name itself is reported on its own line. A warning, not a finding: it reads source text, does not run generators or resolve imports, and does not decide the exit code — `openFootage` refuses a track whose tiles are actually absent | src/lint/tiles.ts:59 | pinned |

## Output (`render` flags — nothing here moves a pixel)

| key | required | default | constraint | source | verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| --format | no | mp4 | mp4 \| webm \| mov \| png-seq. mp4 is libx264 yuv420p; webm is libvpx-vp9 yuv420p with `-b:v 0` so --crf means quality; mov is prores_ks, profile 3 (422 HQ, yuv422p10le); png-seq writes <out>/%06d.png with no ffmpeg in the path and is byte-identical to `frame --at N`. With no --format the --out extension decides; a --format that disagrees with the extension is refused rather than silently winning. Read back with ffprobe in tests/format.test.ts | src/render/encode.ts:106 | pinned |
| --alpha | no | off | asks the codec for an alpha channel: mov becomes ProRes 4444 (yuva444p10le in, yuva444p12le out — the 4444 bitstream is 12-bit), webm becomes yuva420p and the container gains alpha_mode=1 while the stream's own pix_fmt stays yuv420p, png-seq always carries all four channels. Refused for mp4, whose yuv420p has no alpha plane. The channel carries the picture: the rasteriser clears to transparent black (patches/0014), so a pixel no declared ground reaches has alpha 0 and a composition with a full-bleed ground is 255 everywhere — `render` measures and prints the floor rather than restating this | src/render/encode.ts:169 | pinned |

## Layout findings (`layout --json` `findings[]`)

| key | required | default | constraint | source | verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| text_not_painted | no | — | a named-or-text node emitted no geometry at this frame: faded out, zero-sized, or under an ancestor at opacity 0. Normal at any frame outside the node's window; excused by layoutAllow `occlusion` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| text_occluded | no | — | a named-or-text node emitted geometry and no pixel of it survived — something painted over it. Excused by layoutAllow `occlusion` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| panel_out_of_canvas | no | — | the canvas clamped the node's box to zero extent against one of its edges — it is wholly off screen. Layout clips every rect to the viewport before anything can read it, so a PARTIAL overhang leaves no trace and this says nothing about one. Excused by layoutAllow `canvas` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| escaped_container | no | — | the node's box leaves the box of its nearest ancestor that has one. Not reported when that ancestor fills the canvas, because `panel_out_of_canvas` is the reading for that edge. Excused by layoutAllow `overflow` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| content_overlap | no | — | two NAMED nodes on screen whose boxes share positive area, neither an ancestor of the other and neither containing the other. Containment is the ordinary stacking relation (text over a background) and is not reported; sharing an edge is not overlapping. Reported against both, and an allowance on either excuses the pair. Excused by layoutAllow `overlap` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| text_box_overflow | no | — | the node's INK reaches outside its own border box — the glyph run is wider or taller than the box layout gave it. Measured in pixels by hiding the node, not from an advance table. Excused by layoutAllow `overflow` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
| clipped_text | no | — | the node's box crosses its container's edge and its ink stops AT that edge — an `overflow-hidden` ancestor scissored the rest away. Excused by layoutAllow `overflow` | src/render/findings.ts | probed |
